output.title: Naming conventions are a workflow constraint, not a nice-to-have
output.body:
If you run a small business, naming conventions are not cosmetic. They are a design constraint on whether a workflow can move cleanly between your CRM, inbox, invoicing tool, and spreadsheets without someone renaming fields by hand. That matters when you are deciding whether to keep the work manual, hire for it, or invest in bounded automation.

The practical question is simple: when data moves across tools, are the names consistent enough for a person, rule, or AI prompt to understand the same thing every time? If customer IDs, invoice numbers, or lead statuses change format from one system to the next, you do not just get tidy filing problems. You get translation work, and translation work has to be paid for somewhere.

If naming affects invoice matching or payment routing, keep the boundary clear: human approval stays mandatory for any money movement.

A useful next step is to pick one recurring workflow this week — customer enquiries, lead tracking, or invoice processing — and map the field names from source to destination. Write down every place you rename, reformat, or guess. That map is your naming blueprint. If the map is messy, the automation will be too. A tool can only be as tidy as the labels it is handed; labels do not improve by wishful thinking.
